# teleportconnect_cluster (Data Source)

Exposes Teleport cluster metadata, including the cluster TLS CA bundle. The CA bundle is identical for every database in the cluster, so it can be written to a single file (for example to feed a database provider's `sslrootcert`) and reused across multiple database configurations.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Read cluster metadata, including the TLS CA bundle. The CA is the same for
# every database in the cluster, so write it once and reuse the path.
data "teleportconnect_cluster" "this" {}

# Write the (public) CA bundle to a file for a downstream database provider's
# sslrootcert. Lives under .terraform/, which Terraform already ignores.
resource "local_file" "teleport_ca" {
  filename = "${path.root}/.terraform/teleport-ca/teleport-ca.pem"
  content  = data.teleportconnect_cluster.this.ca_certificate
}

output "cluster_name" {
  value = data.teleportconnect_cluster.this.cluster_name
}

output "server_version" {
  value = data.teleportconnect_cluster.this.server_version
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Read-Only

- `ca_certificate` (String) PEM-encoded TLS CA bundle for the cluster. This is public trust material (not a secret); it is the CA that signs the proxy's serving certificate.
- `cluster_name` (String) Name of the Teleport cluster the proxy belongs to.
- `id` (String) Same as cluster_name, exposed as `id` for consistency with Terraform convention.
- `server_version` (String) Teleport server version reported by the proxy.
